failure_summary.description: A sibling endpoint was chosen over the one matching the query's object noun or intent (Zelda Monsters instead of games; Cloud Cast wind speed instead of the 21-day daily forecast; India Today Tag Search with an invented tag instead of Get News; CheapShark List of Deals instead of List of Games). Some of these also dropped the named entity argument.
The 'reviews or ratings' clause got no call (OpenCritic Game Search was never used).
artist_id was placed under required parameters, but the tool lists it as optional and its required list is 'none'.
Each call was wrapped in its own brackets with a stray closing brace, e.g. `[{..}], [{..}], [{..}]}`, so nothing parsed.

The count 'per_page=3' was dropped even though the query said '3 scores on page 1'. Multi-value category was written space-separated instead of comma-separated. Other optionals were dropped or invented.

patch.reasoning: Most failures are wrong sibling-endpoint choices, so the first edit tightens endpoint matching on the object noun and prefers a plain 'get latest' endpoint over a search endpoint with an invented argument. The second fixes the total-parse failure by banning per-call brackets. The third fixes parameter handling: 'Required parameters: none' means everything goes in optional, counts map to count fields, and multiple values are comma-separated. The fourth covers skipped clauses and omitted entity arguments. Noisy or unpredictable gold extras (dice, cards, Lost Ark calls, the dcj9 test tool, quote length limit) are not addressed.

edits.target: Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets.
edits.content: - Exactly one `[` opens and one `]` closes the whole answer. Never wrap each call in its own brackets or separate calls with `], [` (wrong: `[{A}], [{B}]`; right: `[{A}, {B}]`). The answer must end with `}]` immediately followed by `</answer>`, with no extra `}` or `]`.

edits.target: Do not borrow a similar name from a sibling tool (use `region` if the tool has `region`, not `loc`).
edits.content:
- If a tool shows `Required parameters: none`, its `required parameters` list MUST be `[]`. Every value the query supplies, even its main input such as `artist_id` or `lat`/`lon`, goes in `optional parameters`. Never promote an optional-schema parameter to required.
- Count phrases ('15 videos', '3 scores', 'limit to 25', '10 cards per page') always map to the tool's count field (`per_page`, `limit`, `pageSize`, `count`), even when a page number is also given. Several values for one parameter (e.g. science and technology) go in one parameter, comma-separated with no spaces: `science,technology`.

edits.target: Radio stations in a country -> the radio-stations tool, not a Spotify tool.
edits.content:
- Match the query's object noun to the endpoint name, not just the provider or franchise. Read every sibling endpoint of the provider before choosing. 'Games' -> the games-list endpoint, not 'Monsters'. 'Daily forecast for the next few weeks' -> the multi-week daily forecast tool, not a single-metric or current-only tool (wind speed, current weather, air pollution). 'Nearby cities' -> a cities-in-radius tool. 'Active alerts' -> the alerts tool.
- 'Latest news from <source>' with no topic given -> that source's plain 'Get News'/latest endpoint with no required inputs. Do not use a Tag/Search endpoint and invent a tag. Use tag or search endpoints only when the query supplies the topic word.

edits.target: - Do not add 'helper', 'random', 'new releases' or 'list' calls that no clause names.
edits.content: - Every clause needs a call, including soft requests. 'Find its reviews or ratings' -> a review/search tool (e.g. a game-search tool with the game name as `criteria`). When a clause concerns a named entity (game, product, artist) and the tool has a title/name/criteria/keyword field, put that entity in it ('deals for Rocket League' -> a games or deals tool with title `Rocket League`) rather than calling with no arguments. A 'which stores sell...' clause gets its own stores-list call.
